stem.text: The function \( f \) is twice differentiable for all real numbers. Selected values of \( f \) are given in the table. \( \begin{array}{c|cccc} x & 0 & 2 & 5 & 7 \\ \hline f(x) & 4 & -1 & 3 & 6 \end{array} \)

parts.prompt: Must there be a value \( c \), for \( 0 < c < 2 \), such that \( f(c) = 0 \)? Justify your answer.

worked_solution.text: A twice differentiable function is differentiable, hence continuous.
The target value lies strictly between the endpoint values.
By the Intermediate Value Theorem such a c exists.

points.criterion: States that f is continuous on [0, 2] because it is differentiable (or twice differentiable, hence differentiable, hence continuous).
Shows that 0 lies strictly between f(2) = -1 and f(0) = 4, states f is continuous, and answers yes; a named theorem must be the Intermediate Value Theorem.
